sentence: Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic, a medicine that treats infections caused by bacteria.
note: NHS pages: a penicillin antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections.

sentence: The NHS says it is used for chest infections, including pneumonia, and for dental abscesses.
note: NHS: chest infections (including pneumonia) and dental abscesses.

sentence: It is often prescribed for children with ear infections.
note: NHS About amoxicillin: often prescribed for children for ear infections.

sentence: In the UK it is only available on prescription.
note: NHS main page: only available on prescription.

sentence: Antibiotics only work on infections caused by bacteria.
note: Trust leaflet: antibiotics are only effective against bacterial infections.

sentence: They have no effect on viral illnesses such as colds and flu.
note: Trust leaflet: no effect on viral illnesses such as colds and flu.

sentence: The NHS says most adults and children can take amoxicillin.
note: NHS Who can and cannot take: most adults and children can take it.

sentence: For most infections, the NHS says people should feel better within a few days.
note: NHS Common questions: for most infections you should feel better within a few days.

sentence: A doctor or pharmacist decides whether an antibiotic suits a particular infection.
note: General plain fact; no retrieved text states it.

sentence: Different antibiotics are chosen for different types of infection.
note: General plain fact; no retrieved text states it.

sentence: Amoxicillin works by killing the bacteria that cause the infection.
note: NHS Common questions: a penicillin antibiotic that works by killing the bacteria that cause the infection.

sentence: It belongs to the penicillin group of antibiotics.
note: NHS: a penicillin antibiotic.

sentence: A review of antibiotic resistance says penicillins kill bacteria by damaging or blocking the building of the bacterial cell wall.
note: Search summary said a review states penicillins kill bacteria by damaging or inhibiting synthesis of cell walls; the summary did not tie this sentence to a single page, so the review URL is a best attribution.

sentence: More generally, antibiotics either kill bacteria or stop them growing and multiplying.
note: NHS-trust material: antibiotics either kill bacteria or stop them growing and multiplying, by interfering with cell walls or how they make proteins and DNA.

sentence: The NHS advises carrying on until the course is finished, even if the person feels better.
note: NHS Common questions: carry on until you've finished the course, even if you feel better.

sentence: This is because the infection could come back if treatment stops early.
note: NHS: if you stop your treatment early, the infection could come back.

sentence: The NHS says to tell a doctor if there is no improvement after a few days, or if symptoms get worse at any point.
note: NHS: tell your doctor if you do not feel better after taking it for a few days (the page gives a short range), or if you feel worse at any time.

sentence: The NHS says there are no restrictions on food and drink while taking it.
note: Search summary of NHS Common questions: food and drink are unrestricted.

sentence: The NHS lists feeling sick and diarrhoea as the most common side effects.
note: NHS: nausea and diarrhoea are the common side effects.

sentence: Thrush can also develop in some people who take antibiotics, including amoxicillin.
note: NHS side effects page: thrush.

sentence: For thrush, the NHS suggests speaking to a pharmacist or a doctor.
note: NHS: speak to your pharmacist or ask your doctor for advice.

sentence: Rashes can also occur.
note: Search summary of NHS pages and patient leaflets: rashes can occur.

sentence: The NHS says to contact a doctor or NHS 111 straight away for severe diarrhoea, or diarrhoea that contains blood or mucus.
note: NHS: serious side effects, contact a doctor or 111 now: blood or mucus in diarrhoea, or severe diarrhoea.

sentence: The same advice covers signs of liver problems, unusual bruising, or a rash with circular red patches and a high temperature.
note: NHS: signs of liver problems, unusual bruising, rash with circular red patches and high temperature.

sentence: Some of these serious effects can appear after the course has finished.
note: NHS: some can happen for some time (the page gives a number of months) after finishing amoxicillin.

sentence: Delayed allergic reactions can happen several days after starting amoxicillin capsules.
note: NHS: delayed allergic reactions around 7 to 12 days after taking capsules.

sentence: The NHS says these are usually a mild rash, though fever, joint pain and swollen glands can also occur.
note: NHS: usually mild rash; fever, joint pain, swollen glands can also occur.

sentence: In rare cases, amoxicillin can cause a serious allergic reaction called anaphylaxis, which is an emergency.
note: NHS: in rare cases a serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis).

sentence: The NHS says to call 999 if the lips, mouth, throat or tongue swell suddenly, breathing becomes very fast or difficult, or the throat feels tight or swallowing is hard.
note: NHS emergency 999 list.

sentence: Other signs include skin, lips or tongue turning blue, grey or pale, and sudden confusion, drowsiness or fainting.
note: NHS 999 list.

sentence: The NHS says not to drive to A&E in this situation.
note: NHS: do not drive yourself to A&E.

sentence: Patient leaflets say amoxicillin is not for people allergic to amoxicillin or penicillin, or who have had an allergic reaction to any antibiotic.
note: Search summary of emc patient leaflets for amoxicillin.

sentence: The NHS says to tell a doctor first about any past allergic reaction to amoxicillin, penicillin or another medicine.
note: NHS Who can and cannot take amoxicillin.

sentence: Some people carry a penicillin allergy label that may not be accurate, because a rash or stomach upset after antibiotics is sometimes recorded as allergy.
note: Frimley: many patients, especially children, are labelled after a rash or gastrointestinal symptoms; a trust leaflet says symptoms were often due to the infection or side effects. Summary did not tie wording to one page.

sentence: Northern Care Alliance says feeling or being sick is a side effect, not an allergy.
note: Search summary: these are side effects (e.g. nausea, vomiting), this is not allergy.

sentence: NHS trusts describe allergy testing that starts with a review of past symptoms and is offered only when the team judges it safe.

sentence: The NHS says alcohol can be drunk while taking amoxicillin.
note: NHS Common questions: yes, you can drink alcohol while taking amoxicillin.

sentence: Patient leaflets list some medicines that can interact with amoxicillin.
note: Search summaries of emc leaflets and NHS page: interactions listed.

sentence: Allopurinol, a gout medicine, may make an allergic skin reaction more likely.

sentence: Probenecid, another gout medicine, may mean the amoxicillin amount is adjusted.

sentence: Blood thinners such as warfarin may call for extra blood tests.

sentence: Methotrexate may increase side effects, and other antibiotics such as tetracycline may make amoxicillin work less well.
note: Leaflets summary: methotrexate may increase side effects; tetracycline may make it less effective.

sentence: The NHS says amoxicillin does not stop any type of contraception working, including the combined pill, the progestogen-only pill and emergency contraception.
note: NHS Common questions.

sentence: However, being sick or having severe or long-lasting diarrhoea may stop contraceptive pills protecting against pregnancy.
note: NHS: vomiting or severe watery diarrhoea or diarrhoea lasting more than a day (page gives the time) may mean pills do not protect.
